name: Survival English Eval
custom_criteria_prose: This was casual, non-medical, real-life conversation practice (small talk, shops, travel, strangers). Judge everyday spoken English only: natural reactions, follow-up questions, casual register, and comprehension repair. Prefer corrections that replace stiff textbook phrasing with what a real person would actually say. If the AI spoke fast, mumbled, or with a non-US accent, asking for repetition ('sorry?', 'what was that?') is a SKILL to reward, never a weakness. Anki cards should teach natural everyday phrases, reaction words, and polite repair/refusal lines.

anchors.100: Accurate and natural — sounds like everyday speech, not a textbook.
anchors.70: Minor slips that don't affect meaning; occasionally stiff or overly formal phrasing.
anchors.40: Frequent errors or persistently unnatural, translated-sounding phrasing.
anchors.10: Errors so frequent that a stranger would struggle to follow.

anchors.100: Uses fitting everyday wording and completes the conversational job naturally—answering, asking back, choosing, declining, or exiting as the situation requires.
anchors.70: Gets the meaning across with mostly suitable wording but misses an obvious interaction move or sounds somewhat rehearsed.
anchors.40: Limited everyday vocabulary or responses that often do not fit what the other person just said.
anchors.10: Cannot express a usable response to the immediate everyday situation.

anchors.100: Responds with comfortable pacing and smooth turn-taking; short answers remain fully acceptable when the task calls for them.
anchors.70: Meaning is clear despite some searching, pauses, or awkward turn transitions.
anchors.40: Frequent long pauses or abandoned phrases make the exchange hard to sustain.

anchors.100: Follows fast/unclear speech; when lost, repairs naturally ('sorry, what was that?') and confirms key details.
anchors.70: Mostly follows; sometimes answers the wrong question or lets unclear details slide.
anchors.40: Frequent misunderstandings without repair; guesses instead of asking.
anchors.10: Loses the thread constantly and never asks for clarification.
